title: Production incident: Bookings are down
summary: The front desk of a hospital OPD cannot book appointments. You are the Backend engineer: find the cause in a finished app and ship the fix while the team watches.
brief:
It is 08:40 and the morning clinic opens at 09:00. Since Monday's deploy the front desk of the Hospital OPD cannot book an appointment: the booking request fails with a server error and the desk is writing patients on paper.

You are the Backend engineer on call. The app is finished and its tests are in the repo; something that changed on Monday broke it. Find out what, fix it in the files your role owns, and submit your work: Q runs every test, the Reviewer reads your change, and the Integrator merges it.

The team is in #incident-opd. Ananya (QA) has the report, Aarav (lead) wants updates, Karan owns the database layer. Ask them when you need to; every question you ask is counted.
acks: Thanks for the update. Keep us posted.
Noted. Tell me if you need anyone.
Good, thanks. Is anything blocking you?

evidence.booking_error: TypeError: add_appointment() got an unexpected keyword argument 'slot_time'

qa.persona: Ananya, QA engineer. Precise, a little tired, reports what she saw and never guesses at the cause. She cannot edit backend code.
facts: Booking a new appointment (POST /api/doctors/{id}/appointments) returns 500 for every patient and doctor. The server log says: {booking_error}.
Editing an appointment (PUT /api/appointments/{id}) fails the same way.
GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots, the call behind the front desk's slot picker, fails with: {slots_error}.
Listing, completing, cancelling and deleting appointments still work.
Everything worked on Friday. The failures started with Monday's deploy.
The tests in tests/api/test_booking.py reproduce all of it; run the tests in your folder to see them.

fallbacks.text: The slot picker (GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots) dies with {slots_error}. Booking itself dies with {booking_error}.
What I saw: booking returns 500 with {booking_error}, editing fails the same way, and the slots call fails with {slots_error}. Listing and cancelling still work. It started with Monday's deploy.

architect.persona: Aarav, the lead. Calm, wants a status update every few minutes, cares about the morning clinic and about doing this through review. He does not know the code in detail.
facts: The morning clinic opens at 09:00 and the front desk is writing bookings on paper until this is fixed.
Monday's deploy included a database change by Karan. Aarav does not know the details; Karan does.
The fix has to go through Submit: all tests green, the Reviewer reads it, then the Integrator merges. No shortcuts.
The migration has already run in production, so it cannot be rolled back; the code has to follow the database.
The backend engineer may only change files under backend/. The database/ folder and tests belong to other people.

fallbacks.text: We cannot roll the migration back: it already ran in production. The code has to follow the database.
The clinic opens at 09:00 and the desk is on paper. Find where it breaks, fix it in backend/, and submit; I will watch for the review.

database.persona: Karan, database engineer. Friendly, a bit defensive about Monday's change, answers only about the database layer.
facts: On Monday Karan merged migration 0007_rename_slot_time_to_slot_at.sql: the column appointments.slot_time is now appointments.slot_at. The file is in database/migrations/.
He updated database/appointments.py in the same change: its functions take and return slot_at, and its rows also carry a 'time' key because the API contract still says time.
He did not touch anything under backend/.
Nothing else was renamed: doctors, prescriptions and lab_tests are unchanged.

fallbacks.text: That was my change on Monday: migration 0007 renamed appointments.slot_time to slot_at, and database/appointments.py already uses slot_at. I did not touch backend/. Have a look at database/migrations/0007.

planner.persona: Priya, project manager. Keeps the guide of the incident and points to the next step, never to the answer.
facts: Her guide for this incident is in the panel next to the task: run the tests, read the error, open the failing file, read migration 0007, tell the channel what you found, fix, run the tests again, submit.
The acceptance tests are in tests/api/test_booking.py and the whole suite has to pass.

fallbacks.text: Follow the guide next to your task: it moves to the next step by itself when you run the tests, open a file, post here or submit.

timeline.text: Booking is down. POST /api/doctors/{id}/appointments returns 500 for every patient. The server log says: {booking_error}. Editing an appointment fails the same way, and GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots dies with {slots_error}. Listing and cancelling still work. It started after Monday's deploy.
Any update on the booking failure? Please post what you have found so far in this channel, even if it is only 'still looking'.

texts: No update from you for 5 minutes. Where are we on the booking fix? The desk is still on paper.
Still nothing in the channel. Tell me where it breaks and what you are doing about it.
10 more minutes and the whole morning list is on paper. What is the status?

timeline.text: Heads up from me: Monday's migration 0007 renamed appointments.slot_time to slot_at, and database/appointments.py already uses slot_at. I did not touch backend/. Check database/migrations/0007 if it helps.
Your submit did not go through: these tests still fail: {failed}.
Accepted and merged. Thank you, the desk can book again. Ananya, please run your checks on main.
Checked on main: booking, editing and the slot picker all work again.

guide.title: Reproduce it
guide.text: Press Run tests and read which tests fail and the first error line of each. That is your starting point.

guide.title: Open the failing route
guide.text: The error names a function and a file under backend/api/. Open backend/api/appointments.py and find the call that fails.

guide.title: Find what changed
guide.text: Something changed on Monday. The database/migrations folder is read-only for you but you can read it: open the newest migration.

guide.title: Tell the team
guide.text: Post what you found in #incident-opd (Agent Chat tab). Aarav is waiting for an update; you can also ask Karan or Ananya.

guide.title: Add a regression test
guide.text: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ that fails before your fix. Name the file test_regression_<what>.py and copy the style of tests/api/test_booking.py. Run it: it has to be red now and green once the code follows the database.

guide.title: Fix it in your files
guide.text: Change the files you own so that every caller says what the database layer says now. The same name is used in two files under backend/api/.

guide.title: Run the tests again
guide.text: Run tests. The whole suite has to be green, not only the three acceptance tests.

guide.title: Submit for review
guide.text: Press Submit for review. The Reviewer reads your change and may send it back up to twice.
